learningObjectives: Read user input using Java input utilities.
Implement decisions using if, else if, else, and switch.

activities.title: Input-Process-Output Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a simple interactive Java program.

content.concept: A console program commonly reads input, stores or converts the value, processes it using program logic, and displays the result.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Scanner Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a Scanner input statement.

content.concept: Scanner reads input from a source such as System.in. Methods such as nextInt(), nextDouble(), and nextLine() read different forms of input.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The Java utility class used for reading input.
The standard input stream, commonly connected to keyboard input.
The variable referencing the Scanner object.
Declares an integer variable and stores the value returned by nextInt().

activities.title: Condition Matcher
activities.instruction: Choose the condition that correctly represents each requirement.

content.concept: Conditional statements evaluate boolean expressions and select which block of code should execute.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Decision Builder
activities.instruction: Build an if-else structure from the given requirement.

content.concept: An if-else structure evaluates a condition and executes one block when it is true and another block when it is false.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
